title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: A Musical Evening with Decoda & Ringdown featuring Caroline Shaw & Danni Lee Parpan
location: Asheville, NC
description: Decoda and Ringdown take the stage at the Asheville Art Museum for a vibrant, genre-defying evening of music. This special collaboration brings together Decoda, Carnegie Hall’s only affiliate ensemble, with Ringdown for an electrifying evening of chamber music. Featuring celebrated songwriter Danni Lee Parpan and Pulitzer-Prize winning composer and North Carolina native Caroline Shaw, Ringdown bridges classical and contemporary worlds together in a way that feels both expansive and deeply person
source: Asheville Area Chamber of Commerce, Asheville Art Museum

title: A Musical Evening with Decoda & Ringdown ft. Caroline Shaw & Danni Lee Parpan
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
Tuesday, June 16, 2026 | 6:30 pm – 8:00 pm | $30 non-members; $27 Members; $15 students Event Details & Tickets 
Ringdown’s music is like calling your first love on a rotary telephone, percussively tearing out the hammers from a 1924 vintage upright, and flinging each of them into space while you wait for every heartache you’ve ever felt to quietly return. Collaborators Caroline Shaw and Danni Lee Parpan—who between the two of them have a Pulitzer Prize, a handful of Grammys, and a “Best Drum Major Award”—describe Ringdown as an electronic cinematic pop duo based in Portland, Oregon and New York City. Others have described Ringdown as the love child of Johannes Brahms and Brandi Carlile—if they were born in the same century and if Brahms was a queer woman. You decide. 
Decoda is an artist-led chamber music collective dedicated to creating a more compassionate and connected world through music. As the only affiliate ensemble of Carnegie Hall, Decoda combines virtuosic performance with deep community engagement, bringing chamber music to concert halls, schools, shelters, hospitals, and correctional facilities. 
The Asheville Art Museum promises to be a vibrant gathering place where art sparks imagination, broadens perspectives, and connects people across time and cultures. As a cultural institution rooted in community service, we welcome all visitors and embrace practices that encourage mutual respect, foster dialogue, and strengthen community. We are devoted to the art of the United States with a special focus on art from the Southern Appalachian region. We embrace the richness and complexity of the American experience, championing an broad vision of the United States and affirming the power of art to shape and inspire our culture. We strive to enrich and uplift our community by collecting with purpose, collaborating generously, inviting boldly, welcoming warmly, and engaging deeply. ashevilleart.org

title: Live Jazz Tuesday: Jay Sanders, Will Boyd, Zack Page & Alan Hall
location: Little Jumbo, 241 Broadway St, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall distill the pure essence of improvisational expression, converging as alchemists of sound, transmuting musical elements into their most essential forms. This quartet embodies the philosophical concept of quintessence—the fifth element beyond earth, air, fire, and water—representing the fundamental substance from which all musical reality springs. 

Their original compositions crystallize the essential qualities of diverse influences, oscillating between through-composed musical themes, groove-based soul explorations, traditional jazz-influenced pieces, Americana-inspired peaceful melodicism, world music influences, free jazz adventures, and occasional forays into cacophonous noise music. Through years of improvisational study, they’ve learned to access that rarefied space where genres dissolve into pure creative energy. 
In this musical laboratory, Sanders’ guitar becomes a conduit for universal vibration, Boyd’s reeds channel the breath of consciousness itself, Page’s bass provides the fundamental frequency of existence, while Hall’s percussion creates the rhythmic heartbeat of the cosmos. 


Will Boyd – Sax, Flute, Clarinet, EWI
Zack Page – Acoustic & Electric Bass
Alan Hall – Drums
Jay Sanders – Guitar and Effects

Every Monday and Tuesday, Little Jumbo brings live jazz to your ears. littlejumbobar.com

title: AT at Hot Springs to the Rich Mountain Fire Tower; 12.5 mile Fitness Loop Hike.
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**MEETUP OPTIONS:**
8:15 AM To carpool at Weaverville walmart parking, lower level parking on the right. **OTHERWISE,** meet at the trailhead parking area @ 8:55 AM. Right turn just before the bridge at Hot Springs; quick left under the bridge to the riverside parking on the right. Please comment if you plan to carpool.

**DISTANCE:** 12.5- 13 miles.
**ELEVATION GAIN**: Approximately 3,200'.
'
This loop hike begins at the riverside parking area at Silvermine Rd. We will take the AT south to the Rich Mountain Fire Tower (see attached pic) spur and return on the Round Top Trail. The out bound hike {approximately 8 miles} has 2 extended climbs. The first is up and beyond Lover's Leep near Hot Springs, and the second begins at Tanyard Gap to the Fire Tower spur trail (total elevation gain of approximately 3,200'. The return we will take the Round Top Trail to loop back which is a gradual (knee friendly) descent to a left on the French Broad the river road for about 1/2 mile back to the parking area.

**Hike** **Highlights** include beautiful high ridge-line views overlooking the French Broad River Valley (picture), rocky outcrops at Lovers Leap, an old waterfilled tobacco field reservoir, and long range moutain views from the fire tower.

**PACE**: We hike at a steady pace averaging 2.5 MPH on longer climbs with brief regrouping as needed and at trail intersections, and 3- 3+mph pace on level and downhill sections. This is for conditioned hikers. Please know your hiking abilities and be capable of hiking this distance, elevation, and pace, BEFORE SIGNING ON.

**DOGS:** Well-behaved dogs are welcome. There is water available at the reservoir and small active step-over springs. The final phase is along the relatively flat shoulder of the French Broad River).

**RSVP CANCELATION:** IF YOU SIGN UP FOR THIS HIKE, OR THE WAITLIST, and CHANGE YOUR PLANS, CANCEL YOUR RSVP TO FREE UP YOUR RESERVED SPOT FOR OTHER HIKERS. THE WAITLIST REMAINS ACTIVE UNTIL 8 AM HIKE DAY SO YOU MAY BE MOVED ON UNTIL THAT TIME.

**WEATHER**: Cancellation due to weather will be made on or before 7:15 am on the day of the hike.

**\*HIKE LEVELS:**
Level 1: 0-600'; Level 2: 600-900'; Level 3: 900-1200'; Level 4: 1200-1500'; Level 5: 1500-1800'; \*LEVEL 6 1800-2100'; \*LEVEL 7; 2100-2400';
Level 8; 2400-2700'; Level 9; 2700-3000'; Level 10; **3000-4000**';
ULTIMATE HIKES > 4000'

title: Flat Laurel Creek
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
This is one of the most popular creek hikes near Asheville. Note this is not the Flat Laurel Creek Trail, it is a creek hike. It begins at NC Hwy. 215 near the confluence of Flat Laurel Creek and the West Fork of the Pigeon River (35.3283, -82.9093). We will ascend past numerous rapids and a few impressive waterfalls. We will be in the creek or rock hopping most of the day. The requirements are a good sense of balance, comfortable shoes with good traction, and ability or interest to hike and climb in a creek. Good swimming holes abound, and a few waterslides. The pace will be relaxed and we will take a short break one of the many scenic spots for lunch. After finishing the ascent we will trail hike up to the Black Balsam parking lot, where cars will be left for this shuttle. You will have the option to hike up Big Sam Mountain (over 6K) for the view. However, the group will proceed directly to the parking by Black Balsam.

We will climb 800 feet and hike approx. 3 miles.
We will be meeting at the end of Black Balsam Knob Road (FS 816) at the parking lot for the Big Sam trailheaed at 9:30 am. The coordinates are 35.325752, -82.881991.

Any questions I can be reached or text at 828 231-3581.

title: Wednesday night Bent Creek
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
Weather: No rain in forecast, I'll let you know if it's raining, and/or cancelled.
I did this hike series for many years before 2022, but I did it as a high-speed hike, and I am now doing it as a moderate speed hike. This is a numbers limited event and I expect people who sign-up to show up. Late cancellations, and those that don't show up are bumping other interested hikers, and they will not be allowed on future hikes.
If all goes well, I will try to post a hike most weeks, and for days Tue or Wed, distance, and start location, like switching between Hard Times trail-head and Bent Creek River Park, may change.
The current route is about 5.5 miles.
Please folks, this is intended as a moderate paced hike, and we'd like all attendees to keep up with the hike leader(s). This hike is intended as a workout hike for people to get in condition to do weekend hikes.
Moderate paced means 22-24 min miles, or 2 ½ mph.
As such, we do not take breaks, take in views, or snap photos along the way. Please make sure you're able to keep up with the group. This hike has always served as a good chance to get exercise during the week, meet new people, and create interest for weekend enjoyment hikes. It's a great introduction to the AHG family.
No need to RSVP "No" or "not attending" unless changing from a "Yes."
Please read the full description before RSVPing, and only sign up if you are sure you can go. Thanks in advance for keeping your RSVP up-to-date and not being a last-minute cancellation or no-show. This is an ongoing issue with Meetups and often keeps people on waitlists from being able to attend our hikes.
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
Follow signs off of Brevard Rd (Rt 191) to Lake Powhatan Rec Area. The road is Bent Creek Ranch Rd. to Wesley Branch Rd. Follow signs to Lake Powhatan until you come to Hard Times Trailhead on your left, 2.5 miles. It is very clearly marked. Parking is very limited at the trailhead but there’s a paved pull-off just before the Hard Times trailhead and more parking just beyond at the Ledford Branch trailhead. We will access Bent Creek forest by way of Hard Times Trail and do some combination of loop and out and back.
Arrive at the trailhead BY 6:00. Because it is a weeknight hike, we are unable to wait for latecomers, fighting daylight.
\*\*\*If you are running behind, please post a comment on this Meetup page by 5:45 pm. There is no cell service at the parking lot, so if we don't have any advance notice of you running late by 5:45, we can't get any notifications at the trailhead and we will not wait for you.
We start the hike at 6:00, rarely do we get much later than that.
• Wear closed-toed footwear appropriate for hiking. The trail will consist of dirt, rocks, roots, mud and mulch.
• Bring plenty of water.
• Bring rain gear if a chance of rain is in the forecast.
Headlamps suggested
• Dogs on leashes the whole time are welcome. This is an active mountain bike area and it can get messy with dogs running loose among hikers and mountain bikers.
Please make sure to keep your RSVP up-to-date. You don't want to be "that person" who cancels last minute or no-shows and keeps someone from joining in if there's a waitlist. Thanks for your consideration - it is appreciated!
Feel free to post questions not covered in this description in the comments section.
Thanks - we'll see you on the trail!

title: Curator's Talk | The Art of Paper
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us as Susan Gosin and Cynthia Nourse Thompson, two of the three curators of The Art of Paper, will discuss the fascinating realization of this exhibition, which features works by acclaimed artists from the 20th and 21st centuries drawn from the extensive collection of Jordan D. Schnitzer and his Family Foundation.  
Highlights include the evolution of handmade paper art as a progression from and response to the historic relationship between print and paper, revealing another important story about the act of collaboration among artists, fine printers, and hand papermakers at renowned publishing studios.  
Susan Gosin grew up as a member of five generations of commercial papermakers in Wisconsin. After receiving her MFA at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, she cofounded Dieu Donné in New York City in 1976. She has been involved in the field of hand papermaking as an artist, educator, writer, lecturer, and collaborator for fifty years. Her work has been exhibited and collected by institutions such as MoMA, New York; the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York; and the Getty, Los Angeles.   
Cynthia Nourse Thompson is currently Professor and Director of Curatorial Affairs at the Zuckerman Museum of Art at Kennesaw State University. Prior to this position, for six years she was Associate Professor and Director of the graduate programs in Book Arts & Printmaking and Studio Art at University of the Arts in Philadelphia, PA, while also serving as curator for the Joy Pratt Markham Gallery at the Walton Arts Center in Fayetteville, AR. As a curator, Thompson has organized and curated more than 50 exhibitions since 2000. 
Arturo Herrera, Mine, 2007, pigmented abaca watermark on pigmented cotton base sheet with hand-cut collaged
pulp painting, edition 9/23, 60 x 30 inches. © Arturo Herrera, Collection of Jordan D. Schnitzer.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Catawba Falls River and Ridge Loop - 3.6 Mi, 850 Ft EG
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**RSVP opens Sunday, Jun 14th, 8:00 pm**

A shorter hike for this week but I always enjoy Catawba Falls and the challenge of 580 stair steps (equivalent to 30 stories). Some of the stairs and platforms are open metal grate so some people and dogs may not like that but the views are spectacular. We will get a little earlier start as the parking lot and trail can be busy. We will complete our loop by doing the Ridgeline Trail back to the bottom.

https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/north-carolina/catawba-falls-river-loop

Hillmans in Old Fort does open at 11am for lunch and I am planning to go there after the hike.

***Dog Policy:*** Dogs are welcome but must be leashed and okay with open metal grate stairs and platforms.

***Guest Policy:*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they should join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, contact me in advance and ask if it's okay to bring a "+1" after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, I MAY be able to add your guest.

**MEET-UP TIME AND PLACE**
Please either meet at the Catawba Falls parking lot at 9:00 or arrange to carpool with someone in your part of town. I can't figure out a good carpool location for this one, post in the comments if you would like to carpool and what side of town you are located.

**COURTESY TO WAIT-LISTERS (Please abide!)**
Only sign up if you \*TRULY\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers will have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.
If you're on the waiting list, keep checking the evening before. Despite what I wrote above, we always get last-minute dropouts.

**WEATHER**
I'll monitor National Weather Service forecasts for the hike area and email cancellation messages by 7:30 AM if the forecast is for more than a 50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
If you have any questions, message me through MeetUp until 8:00 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy on the trail, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: 508-965-2333.

title: A Day of Music & Art

description:
Join us for a vibrant Day of Art + Music with Decoda and artists from the Decoda Chamber Music Festival (DCMF). This all-ages experience invites you to explore the museum through sound, creativity, and connection.  
Enjoy an interactive performance with Decoda artists, take part in hands-on workshops that blend listening, composing, and visual art-making, and wander the galleries on a self-guided musical tour—where works of art are paired with live performances by DCMF musicians. The day culminates in Arboretum in the Museum, an immersive musical experience in which solo performances unfold simultaneously throughout the space, transforming the museum into a living, breathing soundscape. 
Schedule 
Noon–12:30pm — Live Music on the Plaza 
12:30–1:15pm — Interactive Performance (Decoda Artists) 
1:30–2pm — Creative Art & Music Making & Live Music on the Plaza 
2–2:45pm — Musical Gallery Tour 
2:45–3:15pm — Creative Art & Music Making 
3:30pm — Arboretum in the Museum 
————— 
Decoda is an artist-led chamber music collective dedicated to creating a more compassionate and connected world through music. As Carnegie Hall’s only affiliate ensemble, Decoda pairs virtuosic performance with deep community engagement, bringing chamber music to concert halls, schools, shelters, hospitals, and correctional facilities. 
Each summer in the Asheville region, Decoda leads the Decoda Chamber Music Festival, a dynamic training program for young musicians who seek to develop both artistic excellence and social impact. title: Father's Day Walk of the Western End of Maggie Valley
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at Maggie Methodist, 4192 Soco Rd., Maggie Valley 28751, in the corner of the parking lot closest to Soco Rd., but furthest from the church building. We will meet at 2:00 p.m. There are no restrooms at the start point, so take care of any needs before you arrive.

The walk is pretty flat. Tennis shoes are fine; walking poles aren't needed. Dress appropriately for the weather. Bring lots of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Strollers are fine.

We will walk west on Soco Road to Fie Top, with one or two side excursions. We will cross Soco Road and then walk east on the opposite side of Soco Road as far as Town Hall. We will cross the road and head west again, finally returning to the Start Point.

title: Summer Art Camp | Art Around the World (Rising 3rd – 5th grade)
location: NC
description:

Students will investigate artists and artworks from each continent using a variety of processes and materials. They will explore drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture and collage. During art camp, students will collect artworks to create a portfolio that crosses all continents and cultures from around the world.     
Meet the Instructor: Sarah Medsker
Sarah Medsker has a master’s degree in education and is an art teacher in western North Carolina, having taught students between kindergarten and 8th grade. Teaching children is her passion, as she has been facilitating art-making for over 15 years. When she is not teaching art, she loves traveling, cooking, reading and exploring professional development opportunities in the field of art education.

location: NC
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
 The first two days of this camp will be about tearing up, mashing, blending and laying out paper to dry into curated sheets – cut and folded into books we will make on the following three days.  There are so many ways to make a book! Picture journals with ribbons, folded snake books and bedazzled covers!  
Meet the Instructor: Maggie Imhoff
Maggie Imhoff is an educator of twenty-three years, including, most recently, the Art teacher at Ira B Jones elementary school in Asheville, NC. She has taught at several summer camps, created outdoor art experiences for kids as well as directed at a children’s circus. She loves to celebrate art in her everyday life. She knits, paints, sings, and dances.  This quote from Phylicia Rashad sums it up: “Before a child speaks, it sings.  Before they write, they paint. As soon as they stand, they dance. Art is the basis of human expression.” As an art educator, it brings her joy to bring art to children’s lives.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

AVL Digital Nomads
Are you tired of staring at the same four walls and talking to your houseplants? Remote work has its perks, but the isolation can get old quickly. It is time to reclaim your social and professional capital while getting some serious work done.

AVL Digital Nomads is heading to The Workspace at 7Acres for two free coworking days. This is the newest and most highly anticipated workspace in Asheville, and our nomad community has an exclusive invite to test drive it.

**The Headlines**
Here is what you can look forward to at your temporary headquarters:

* Limited-distraction, dedicated desks to help you actually focus.
* Powered raising and lowering desks so you can stretch your legs throughout the day.
* Multiple monitors and docking stations to maximize your productivity.
* Ergonomic chairs because your back deserves better than the kitchen stool.
* Blazing fast 2gig WiFi that puts standard home internet to shame.

**A Bigger Vision for a Life Well Lived**
This is not just another office space with a gym next door. The Workspace is only the first phase of Seven Acres, a community built around a much bigger idea. The founders believe that work, play, recovery, and connection are all essential to a fulfilling life. Everything here is intentionally designed to make each element better, creating one cohesive community. You can learn all about this vision during your visit.

**The Logistics**
This event marks day ONE of two free coworking days. You are welcome to drop in for one day or join us for both. Plus, make sure to stick around for a separate social time at the end of the day on Thursday to celebrate, unwind, and connect with fellow nomads. When you show up, say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once you’re all settled, take some time to chat with your fellow writers. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

title: Test Drive Asheville’s Newest Work Oasis: Free Coworking at 7Acres (2)
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Are you tired of staring at the same four walls and talking to your houseplants? Remote work has its perks, but the isolation can get old quickly. It is time to reclaim your social and professional capital while getting some serious work done.

AVL Digital Nomads is heading to The Workspace at 7Acres for two free coworking days. This is the newest and most highly anticipated workspace in Asheville, and our nomad community has an exclusive invite to test drive it.

**The Headlines**
Here is what you can look forward to at your temporary headquarters:

* Limited-distraction, dedicated desks to help you actually focus.
* Powered raising and lowering desks so you can stretch your legs throughout the day.
* Multiple monitors and docking stations to maximize your productivity.
* Ergonomic chairs because your back deserves better than the kitchen stool.
* Blazing fast 2gig WiFi that puts standard home internet to shame.

**A Bigger Vision for a Life Well Lived**
This is not just another office space with a gym next door. The Workspace is only the first phase of Seven Acres, a community built around a much bigger idea. The founders believe that work, play, recovery, and connection are all essential to a fulfilling life. Everything here is intentionally designed to make each element better, creating one cohesive community. You can learn all about this vision during your visit.

**The Logistics**
This event marks day TWO of two free coworking days. You are welcome to drop in for one day or join us for both. Plus, make sure to stick around for a separate social time at the end of the day on Thursday to celebrate, unwind, and connect with fellow nomads. Register for day [ONE here](https://www.meetup.com/avl-digital-nomads/events/315228909/).

Come build community, upgrade your workday, and help each other thrive. We can't wait to see you there!

**ADN Pirani Cups available**
Celebrate our 5th anniversary with our customized [ADN Pirani cups](https://avldigitalnomads.org/meet-our-brand-new-customized-adn-pirani-mugs/)! Available in 16oz, 26oz, and 32oz sizes, you can purchase yours directly at this event.

title: Sip, Snack, and Scout: ADN Takes Over 7Acres
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Let’s be honest. Your living room walls are starting to talk back, and your houseplants are terrible conversationalists. It is time to reclaim your social capital and see what the future of flexible work actually looks like.

Join AVL Digital Nomads as we celebrate the finale of our two free coworking days with an evening social mixer at the brand-new Workspace at 7Acres.

Most places give you one thing, like a desk and a sad coffee maker. 7Acres is doing something entirely different. They are launching a visionary space built around the idea that work, play, recovery, and connection are all critical to a life well lived. This isn't just a gym co-located next to an office. It is one organization, one intention, and one community intentionally designed to make every part of your day better.

You can learn all about the grand vision during your visit, but this night is mostly about kicking back.

**What is on tap?**

* **The Fuel:** Enjoy complimentary adult beverages and light snacks while you mingle.
* **The Grand Tour:** Get a firsthand look at the first phase of this exciting new concept.
* **The Loot:** We are hosting raffles for 7Acres memberships alongside some excellent discount opportunities.

Just want to chill? You are completely welcome to simply show up, grab a drink, and enjoy the vibe. There is no pressure to talk shop. This is a welcoming, interesting venue designed for real human connection.

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: The Foundation
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
All of life comes to me with ease, joy and glory™

The three and a half day Foundation class is designed to break the foundation of what you think your reality is, so you can create the reality that works for you.

The Foundation class is designed to empower you to change anything and everything you’d like to change in your life. You will be given a whole toolbox that will allow you to break apart the foundation of limitation that we so often function from and build a new foundation, one of limitless possibility so that you can begin to create the life you truly desire.

What do you desire? What would you like to be different? Would you like more joy? More fun? More ease? Would you like to wake up in the morning with a sense of gratitude... happy to be on the planet?

Whatever it is for you, it is possible. Thousands of people around the world have created the life they desire by using the simple and pragmatic tools of Access Consciousness® that you will be introduced to in the Foundation class.

Everything can change.
Anything is possible.
The question is, will you choose it?

title: Book + Art | Glorious Country: Frederic Church and the Celebration of the American Landscape
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
In this richly illustrated talk, Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award finalist Victoria Johnson shares the dramatic and consequential life of the artist Frederic Church (1826–1900), whose footsteps she followed around the globe for her “absorbing” (Ron Chernow) and “superb” (Publishers Weekly) new biography of Church, Glorious Country. Church’s curiosity, bravery, and passion for nature drove him to explore the world, but it was his astonishing talent that allowed him to bring the world to America at a time when landscape photography was in its infancy and most of his fellow Americans would never see a different country or continent. Among Church’s many destinations was Western North Carolina, where he painted along the French Broad River. Exhibited to acclaim abroad, Church’s blockbuster paintings persuaded skeptical European critics that the New World could, in fact, give birth to towering artists and furnish the subject matter for great art. At Olana, Church’s estate on the Hudson River, he forged an enduring masterpiece of architectural, interior, and landscape design. A master artist and citizen, Church brought the world to America, and America to the world. 
Presented in Frederic Church’s bicentennial year. 
About the Speaker
Victoria Johnson is the author of three books, including the Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award finalist American Eden: David Hosack, Botany, and Medicine in the Garden of the Early Republic. She holds a doctorate in sociology from Columbia University and an undergraduate degree in philosophy from Yale. She is Professor of Urban Policy and Planning at Hunter College of the City University of New York.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Frida Kahlo
location: NC
description:
Frida Kahlo is a phenomenon. She is arguably the world’s favourite female artist—beloved by young and old. Exhibition on Screen’s award-winning film—first released during covid to a restricted audience – is back by popular demand with an exciting new addition from the curators of the blockbuster transatlantic exhibition from Tate Modern and MFA Houston ‘Frida Kahlo: the Making of an Icon’. 
Who was Frida Kahlo? Everyone knows her face but who was the woman behind the bright colours, the big brows and the floral crowns? Take a journey through the life of a true icon, discover her art, and uncover the true story of her rebellious, passionate and turbulent life. 
Making use of the latest technology to deliver previously unimaginable quality, we take an in-depth look at key works throughout her career. Using letters Kahlo wrote to guide us, this definitive film reveals her deepest emotions and unlocks the secrets and symbolism contained within her art. 
Exhibition on Screen’s trademark combination of interviews with world experts and a detailed exploration of her art, with new special bonus footage from the curators of the blockbuster 2026 exhibition, delivers a treasure trove of colour and emotion. This personal and intimate film offers privileged access to her works, her home, her studio and highlights the source of her feverish creativity, her resilience and her unmatched lust for life, beauty and revolution. 
Created in close collaboration with world experts and those who knew her. Featuring additional new material from the curators of the groundbreaking new Tate Modern and MFA Houston exhibition. Directed by Ali Ray.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Historic Columbia SC Morning Walk—Governor's Mansion, Finlay Park, and More!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at 10:00 a.m. in the lobby of the Hampton Inn, 822 Gervais Street, Columbia 29223 (enter the lobby from the Lincoln Street side). Restrooms are available at the start point.

The trail takes you past the Woodrow Wilson Boyhood Home, around the Governor's Mansion, through the newly reopened Finlay Park, and through Memorial Park.

There are some moderate hills and stair climbing, but it is almost entirely on pavement. Tennis shoes are fine; some may want walking sticks or hiking boots.

Dress for the weather. It will likely be very hot. A hat and sunscreen are highly recommended.

**Plenty of water** and a protein snack are advised as always. Wheelchairs are not recommended, although strollers ought to be ok. Dogs are welcome.

Our Meetup group offers some version of this walk every three months. It's that good! You will surely enjoy it.

Traditionally, many of us eat at Five Guys (near the start point) after the walk. There are lots of other restaurants nearby. Give yourself plenty of time to enjoy your meal after you join the group for the walk.

About Guest DJ Karen Funshine
Karen Funshine (Karen Smith) has been dancing since age 3, with movement as her lifelong ally. A veteran raver & EDM enthusiast, she was delighted to discover 5Rhythms and ecstatic dance 10 years ago in Austin - a sober and judgment-free space to get wild & free. She’s since facilitated many women’s conscious dance circles and a vibrant live-instrument dance - weaving music and somatic movement to alchemize emotion, open the heart, and awaken joy. Recently relocated to Asheville, Karen is honored to share her passion and playfulness with her beautiful new community through the universal language of music and dance.

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles! We will either be in the large room inside or out back on the patio depending on weather.

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. Feel free to share as much or as little as you want! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:
Asheville Tech Events
Drupal Camp Asheville is an annual two-day conference that focuses on hands-on training and knowledge sharing for all levels of Drupal experience, with a bonus community day spent together in nature.

Drupal is a popular free open-source modular framework and content management system (CMS). It is used to build everything from personal blogs to enterprise applications. Millions of businesses, government agencies, and nonprofit organizations use Drupal because it is free and flexible. It is constantly being improved by the hundreds of thousands of dedicated developers that are part of the global Drupal Community.

The size of our camp is perfect for being able to access session speakers and even do your first session presentation. We are a welcoming event for people at all levels of Drupal knowledge and experience. Come learn and share in an awesome, laid-back environment.

Find all of the info about programming and tickets at https://www.drupalasheville.com.

title: Summer Art Camp | Appalachian Arts & Crafts (Rising 9th - 12th grade)
location: NC
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Blending creativity with cultural heritage, students will explore the artistic traditions of Appalachian culture through a series of hands-on crafts. They will begin the week creating vibrant painted barn quilts and learning basic weaving techniques with natural materials. They’ll spend the remainder of the week further developing their weaving skills to make reed baskets and needle felting a landscape.   
Meet the Instructor: Kati Robbins
Kati Robbins has over 12 years of experience as an art educator, teaching studio arts and crafts to a wide range of age groups in different learning environments. She is currently based in Asheville where she works as a high school art teacher. Her creative work focuses on mixed media and assemblage, with a strong interest in collaborative and community based projects. She is inspired by Appalachian craft traditions, natural materials and the surrounding landscape. When Kati isn’t teaching or making art, she enjoys gardening, cooking, reading and hiking in the mountains.

title: Summer Art Camp | Exploring Photography Without a Camera (Rising 9th – 12th grade)
location: NC
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Photography doesn’t always require a camera. In this experimental image lab, students will explore photography-based processes that use light, chemistry, and transfer techniques to create images. Through hands-on exploration of cyanotypes, lumen prints, pinhole photography, and image transfers, students will experiment with transparency, layering, and transformation—creating works that blur the line between photography, printmaking, and mixed media.     
Meet the Instructor: Kristina Shriver
Kristina Shriver is a visual art educator with over 16 years of experience, working with students of all ages. She teaches at Asheville High School and serves as an AP Studio Art Reader and mentor for other art educators. Kristina designs hands-on, material-rich art experiences that connect historical techniques to contemporary practice, emphasizing experimentation, personal storytelling, and meaningful creative exploration.

title: Curator's Talk | Hidden in Plain View—Art in Southern Appalachia
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Co-creator of Warp, Weft and the Grid, Kathleen Curtis Wilson 
Curator Kathleen Curtis Wilson will present a series of photographs and share personal stories about her collection of bed coverlets woven by women in southern Appalachia, 1850-1930. An appreciation of Appalachian weaving was hindered by stereotypical images of Appalachia as a poverty-ridden, art-poor region. These images and a lack of women’s material culture studies in the region once made it easy to dismiss Appalachia as void of objects of art, creativity, and design worthy of national attention. 
Today, graphic artists and laypersons will appreciate the simple designs of early coverlet patterns for the straight lines, accuracy, and bold color choices of this distinctive artistic tradition. 
The woven coverlets images presented during Wilson’s presentation make it apparent that many southern Appalachian weavers did not put away their looms in the nineteenth century but made a conscious decision to continue to weave and preserve beautiful objects for their own pleasure, as gifts for family members, or in celebration of important events. 
Kathleen Curtis Wilson is the author of five non-fiction books: The Quiet Work of Women (2001, reprinting 2026); Uplifting the South—Mary Mildred Sullivan’s Legacy for Appalachia (2005); Irish People, Irish Linen (2011); Dancing at the Warm Springs Hotel (2022); and Adventurous Max Flax (2023), an educational children’s book. Her first novel, The Fabric of Wishful Thinking. (available 2026). 
Wilson served as honorary fellow at both University of Ulster, Northern Ireland, and Virginia Humanities, Charlottesville, Virginia. She has given scores of public speeches and lectures at professional conferences in the United States and abroad. Born in Michigan, Wilson studied weaving at The Cranbrook Schools. She established and operated Old Abingdon Weavers in Southwest Virginia from 1983-1993. She lives in Blacksburg, Virginia

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Book + Art | The Fabric of Wishful Thinking
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join Kathleen Wilson, co-curator of Warp Weft & the Grid, for an introduction to her debut novel, The Fabric of Wishful Thinking. 
This richly researched portrait of 1910 rural Appalachia is written by an author with deep expertise in Appalachian history, craft, and culture. Along with its compelling story, Wilson’s book offers a rare look inside early Southern textile mill culture. The Fabric of Wishful Thinking is a powerful story about families and the fractures that result from divided loyalties. Ella Hutchinson’s story offers a portrait of female resilience during a time without legal protections for mothers and wives. It is a gripping novel about friendship, motherhood, first love, and irrevocable loss.

title: Biltmore Estate: Walk the Westover Green and Blue Trails
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Located at The Inn on Biltmore Estate, the Westover Green and Blue Trails provide access to some of Biltmore's beautiful woodlands. We will loop the Green Trail in a clockwise direction, pick up the Blue Trail to walk its entire length, and then go back to get the rest of the Green Trail.

I estimate this to be about 4.5 miles. The Green Trail is wide. The Blue Trail is of moderate width. These are relatively easy trails. There is a little elevation change, but nothing particularly strenuous.

When you drive to the Inn, you will turn onto its access road. Near the entrance to the Inn is the entrance to the parking area. There are two rows of parking, an upper row closer to the Inn, and a lower row a little further from the Inn. We will gather on the lower row at the far end (away from the Inn).

If you need a restroom prior to the walk, Antler Hill is very close and there are public restrooms there. No restroom facilities are available during the walk.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case you will probably want light hiking boots. Most won't want walking sticks, though I plan to take just one. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers designed for trail use would be ok.

There is a grounds admission fee. We walk at Biltmore several times each year, so an annual grounds pass is highly recommended.

Many regular Biltmore guests have never walked the Westover Trails. I think you will enjoy these.

title: Copperhead Trail at Haywood Community College on National Ice Cream Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
It's likely to be hot, so at the end of the walk we will go get an ice cream together.

To get to the Copperhead Trail from our start point, we will go clockwise on the Bobcat Trail, and then take the Kingfisher Trail to the Copperhead Trail. When we intersect with the Millpond Connector, we will turn left, finishing the campus loop on the Bobcat Trail. All together, it isn't over 2 miles. Part of the walk is on pavement, part on well-groomed trail, and part on not-as-well groomed trail. There is some small elevation change.

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring one walking stick, just in case. As always, you are urged to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have any problem. There are no bathrooms available on a Sunday afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

description:

Routes-

RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.

Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Game Night @ Archetype West Asheville
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
\*\*This is a collaboration with the Asheville's Bored Game Geeks\*\*

Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!
**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville on National Ice Cream Sandwich Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 counterclockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks. Bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

Since it is National Ice Cream Sandwich Day, at the end of the walk we will have available free ice cream sandwiches for our walkers. Now, how's that for a hot summer afternoon!

title: 5 KM/3 mile Sunday Afternoon Walk in Canton
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The start/finish point is the parking lot for the Rec Park baseball field (not to be confused with the public-school baseball field next to the football stadium—our meeting place is a little further down the road). The field has been rebuilt since Hurricane Helene, and the parking area is still there. Hopefully, some of the Clyde Elementary School Cardinals Elite Walking Team and their families will be joining us for this event.

We will start our walk at the Canton Recreation Park, go past Pisgah High School, up to the public library and the historic cemetery, down Academy Street, and through part of downtown on our way back to Canton Greenway and the start point. The up and down are fairly steep.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen. Tennis shoes are fine. This is all pavement, but some might want walking sticks for the up and down; I plan to walk with a pair of walking sticks. Bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome. Some of the sidewalk along well-traveled roads is narrow and some is not in the best condition, so strollers and wheelchairs are not recommended.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.
