title: Walk the Ethnobotany Trail and More at the NC Arboretum
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center which opens at 9:00 a.m. Restrooms are available at the start point. We will start walking as soon as everyone has arrived, hopefully no later than 9:05.

The walk is a guided 5 KM trail. There are some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. Some people will want walking poles.

We will walk down Running Cedar Road to Bent Creak Road. Going down Bent Creek Road, we will turn onto the Ethnobotany Trail, and then back onto Bent Creek Road. We will go back up Wesley Branch Trail to the Willow Pond and thence back to the start point.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome but are not allowed in buildings or in the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $25 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend the driver purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher-level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

title: Access Bars® Class
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
You must be present for the entire class in order to be certified as a Bars Practitioner (BP).

The first class in Access Consciousness is The Bars®. There are 32 points on your head which, when gently touched, effortlessly and easily release anything that doesn’t allow you to receive. It’s like hitting the delete button on your computer. All of the thoughts, feelings, and emotions that keep you stuck, that keep you repeating the same patterns in your life over and over again, are released.

Did you know there are 32 points on your head which, when gently touched, effortlessly and easily release anything that doesn’t allow you to receive? These points contain all the thoughts, ideas, beliefs, emotions and considerations that you have stored in any lifetime. This is an opportunity for you to let go of everything!

Thousands of people have used Access Bars™ to change many aspects of their body and their life, including sleep, health and weight, money, sex and relationships, anxiety, stress and so much more. At worst you will feel like you have just had a phenomenal massage. At best your whole life can change into something greater with total ease.

Registration: https://www.consciousbeing.institute/event-details/asheville-nc-access-bars-class-august-2026

This class will be held at a local Asheville pavilion in a park. The exact location will be determined closer to the event date.

That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Body Process Class: Circuitry
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
## What If Your Body Has Been Waiting for This?

## **You’re Invited: Access Consciousness Body Process Class**

What if your body isn’t something to fix…
but something to listen to?

What if it has been whispering (or maybe shouting) for your attention in ways you were never taught to understand?

I’d love to invite you to a beautiful, hands-on **Access Consciousness Body Process class** — a space where you get to receive, gift, and explore a different communion with bodies.

### What Is a Body Process?

Access Consciousness Body Processes are gentle, hands-on techniques that invite the body to:
• Release stored trauma and shock
• Activate natural capacities
• Undo limitations held in tissue and cellular memory
• Restore communication between you and your body

This isn’t massage.
It isn’t energy work in the traditional sense.
It’s a conversation — with the body.
And bodies respond.

### In This Class You Will:

✨ Learn a specific Access Body Process you can use for life
✨ Both gift and receive the process (yes, you get sessions too!)
✨ Explore how judgment impacts the body
✨ Discover new tools for ease, vitality, and awareness
✨ Leave certified to practice this body process on others

No prior experience is required. Just a body. And a willingness.

### What Becomes Possible?

Many people report:
• Increased ease in chronic patterns
• Greater relaxation and presence
• Changes in long-held physical limitations
• A deeper sense of trust with their body

But more than anything — possibility.
What if your body has capacities you’ve never been shown how to access?

Spots are limited only by space - the sooner you sign up the sooner we can look for larger locations if required.

If you’ve been asking for more ease, more connection, more *aliveness* — this may be the invitation your body has been waiting for.

Would your body enjoy this?

A body process class is a way to experience a new energy. Each is uniquely different and contributes to the being. There are NO contraindications - if it pulls you in it's right for you that day.

This class will include the body process **Circuitry**!

title: Walk 3 Short, Easy Trails at Panther Creek State Park TN
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Panther Creek State Park is in Tennessee, just outside of Morristown. **We will meet at the entrance to the park.** The park covers approximately 1435 acres and is located on the shores of Cherokee Lake. The park offers a variety of recreational opportunities including camping, fishing, boating, picnicking, swimming, hiking, biking, and horseback riding.

The park boasts over 30 miles of world-class trails ranging from easy to difficult. Visitors are encouraged to Leave No Trace when using the trails. Hikers can enjoy a magnificent view of Cherokee Lake and the Cumberland Mountains.

We will do 2 hiking only trails and 1 hiking and biking trail. We will have to travel from trailhead to trailhead. I've tried to factor that into our time.

The Road to Recycling Trail is a 1.2 mile, easy, hiking only trail. This self-guided trail educates park visitors on the benefits of conserving natural resources. As such, there are signs along the trail. This trail was awarded the Governor's Greenways and Trails Stewardship Award in 2004.

The Seven Sinkholes Trail is a 0.6 mile loop, easy, hiking only trail. Sinkholes develop when rainfall dissolves the under-layer of porous limestone rock forming cavities. These cavities and depressions within the limestone gradually enlarge creating sinkholes. The trail meanders around seven distinct sinkholes before dipping into a lush valley of cedar and pine.

Old Wagon Trail is a 1 mile, easy, hiking and mountain biking trail. It appears on the map to be out-and-back 1 mile each way. It is the most popular trail at the park and is excellent for all ages and abilities. This trail follows the contour of Panther Creek and features a flat, wide surface. This is an excellent trail for the wildlife enthusiast, as many different birds and animals are frequently observed along the trail, especially in the early morning.

The park has restrooms in certain areas which we can visit before, between, and after the 3 walks. Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. I believe tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained recently, in which case you will probably want light hiking boots. Most won't want walking sticks, though I plan to take just one. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. I have no information on limitations on dogs (although a park that has horses could hardly complain about dog owners who cleans up their pets' messes). Being easy trails, I would think trail strollers would work. Wheelchairs would probably work on Old Wagon Trail, although I'm not 100% certain.

I have no information on an entrance fee to the park. Come prepared just in case. The walk itself is free.

As you may surmise, I have not done this event previously. You are invited to come and try out this new place with me.
